### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **34** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 03b4d2d1f49fdb8cc4f0004724979305d8902266`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 54 pages)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 03b4d2d1f49fdb8cc4f0004724979305d8902266` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `57dd04ec8d987cff7bb8a7b4c056dbdde1d29a57` — the merge of head `9e4688fb2f85c9c920b047ff5ba0825b14b880a7` into base `03b4d2d1f49fdb8cc4f0004724979305d8902266`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 57dd04ec8d987cff7bb8a7b4c056dbdde1d29a57 && git checkout 57dd04ec8d987cff7bb8a7b4c056dbdde1d29a57
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 03b4d2d1f49fdb8cc4f0004724979305d8902266 9e4688fb2f85c9c920b047ff5ba0825b14b880a7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 03b4d2d1f49fdb8cc4f0004724979305d8902266 && git merge --no-ff 9e4688fb2f85c9c920b047ff5ba0825b14b880a7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 03b4d2d1f49fdb8cc4f0004724979305d8902266
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 03b4d2d1f49fdb8cc4f0004724979305d8902266` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0695d5ce8169a39f13dbda89a6f9b9ffdf68609e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + none

Read, not reviewed (code outside the diff, on the head's tree): `packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts` (`registerFlow`, `execute`), `flow-registration-checks.ts`, `runtime-identity.ts`, `builtin/{index,logic-nodes,parallel-node,subflow-node,map-node,wait-node,screen-nodes}.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` (`canWriteObject`), `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`. The pin test, the two generated baselines and the changeset are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- New optional member `IAutomationService.dryRun?` and 13 new exported types: additive, right. No existing member, type or code changes value.
- Optional is right: every member past `execute` and `listFlows` is optional on the tree (`registerFlow?` at L1650 through `inspectConsumedSuspension?`).
- `FlowDryRunRefusalCode` is an `Extract` of existing `AutomationResult.code` members: no code minted, right. One member is dead in this method (finding 4).
- `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` carry exactly the 13 new names: right.
- Check-runs on the head: every completed run is `success` or `skipped` (Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint PM dispatch-gates, tooling self-tests among them). Build Core, Type Check, Lint and the Test Core / Test UI shards were still `in_progress` when read, so they are not yet verdicts; nothing was re-run here.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch with `Metadata-protocol: none` matches what the diff publishes (no authorable key; AGENTS.md §3). Clause-②: yes (widening) is right: one new optional method and new exported types, nothing narrowed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` (report 6893351705): rule 1 refuses a `runAs: 'system'` draft of type `autolaunched`, `record_change` or `schedule` for every named user. **Escalated to the maintainer, not a must-fix on this PR.** The contract states the consequence honestly, as its own sentence ("is refused for every named user"), and it follows the card's verbatim line from #33661 ("A `runAs: 'system'` definition follows the same admission rule as a by-name start"). What the maintainer should see before #33661 builds on it: (a) rule 1's stated reason in `flow-start-admission.ts` is that a by-name start of such a flow would run elevated from a door that is "wiring, not a design"; a dry run is never elevated and arms nothing, so the reason does not carry over; (b) the flow schema's own text tells authors to declare `runAs: 'system'` on a run with no trigger user, which is every `schedule` flow with a data node and any `record_change` flow fired by a system write, so this is not a corner; (c) the refusal message a maker gets is the by-name one ("This caller may not start this flow. A flow that runs on its own trigger starts there…"), which says nothing about a dry run. Option B in the report (admit, still never elevated) is a later widening of this contract, so landing as ruled does not close it off.
- Dev deviations (signed HTML comment in the PR body, no labels sent): process, no effect on the contract.
- Readings beyond the order, each judged in ④: `script` as outbound ACCEPT; `subflow`/`map` stop ACCEPT; `not_simulated` ACCEPT with finding 3; `'failed'` status ACCEPT with finding 5; writes not judged by validation ACCEPT with finding 2; outbound binds no output ACCEPT with finding 5; `'refused'` meaning ACCEPT.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, against the card's four design questions, the tree it cites, and its first consumer #33661.

Holds on the tree: the three admission rules, their order and the single `PERMISSION_DENIED` code match `flowStartRefusal`; the AI-account rule matches `isAiServiceAccount` with `door.aiExposed` false; grants are resolved by run setup for a context that carries none; `supportsPause: true` is declared by `screen`, `wait`, `subflow`, `map` and the approvals plugin's two nodes; the decision step's `branch` / `'default'` match the executor; `AUTOMATION_UNSCOPED_RUN_DATA_ACCESS` is unreachable with a required `userId`; the options pick only keys `AutomationContext` has and omit `positions`, `permissions`, `posture`, `email`, `runAs`.

Findings:

1. **must-fix. The start condition has no answer.** Live `execute` evaluates the start node's `condition` before any node runs and, when it does not hold, returns `{ success: true, output: { skipped: true, reason: 'condition_not_met' } }` (`engine.ts` ~L7660-7676). `options.record` and `options.previous` exist to feed exactly this gate. The contract never mentions it, and the closed result cannot express it: `'completed'` is defined as "the run reached an `end` node", and `'refused'` takes one of three codes, none of which fits. "This flow would not start for this record" is the first thing a maker dry-running a record-change draft needs to be told. Add the sentence and a representable outcome.
2. **must-fix. The permission promise is wider than the tree can keep.** "A permission refusal is the exception: the step carries, in `refusal`, the refusal the named user would meet for that operation on that object or row." No write is made, so the refusal must come from a preview. The tree's preview primitive, `canWriteObject` (`plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` ~L3690-3750), says in its own doc that `true` never means the write will succeed and that it cannot judge row-level and post-image refusals (the RLS `using` pre-image, the `check` post-image, controlled-by-parent, the tenant post-image), provenance gates, or the `owner_id` forge; it takes `insert | update` only, so there is no delete arm; and it answers a boolean, not a `FlowInnerRefusal`. A step with no `refusal` would read as "this user may do it" when the dry run could not know. The order's rule for this case was to stop and raise it as `needs_decision`. Bound the sentence to what a preview can judge and say which refusals a dry run may not report.
3. **should-fix. The routing class names two node types the engine does not run and omits one it does.** `parallel_gateway` and `join_gateway` are BPMN interop ids with no executor anywhere in `service-automation/src`; the shipped node is `parallel` (`builtin/parallel-node.ts`, registered in `builtin/index.ts`). As written, a `parallel` block is "outside every class named here" and stops the run as `not_simulated`, and the sentence "run as the live run runs them" is vacuous for the two gateways. Name `parallel`; and say how "one ordered step list" orders steps from concurrent branches and from an inclusive decision's fan-out.
4. **should-fix. `FLOW_NO_START_NODE` cannot occur.** The second answer throws for any definition `registerFlow` would refuse, and registration refuses a flow with no `start` node (`flow-registration-checks.ts` L276; `engine.ts` L7650 calls the execute exit unreachable for that reason). So the third answer's `FLOW_NO_START_NODE` and its union member are dead. Removing a member after publication is a narrowing; drop it now, or say which of the two answers wins.
5. **should-fix. `'failed'` claims "the live run would fail there too", which the contract's other sentences make false.** A dry run can fail where the live run would not: a later node reads an outbound node's output that the dry run left unset; a never-elevated `runAs: 'system'` draft meets a refusal the published flow would not (the Identity section says so itself); a filtered read does not see a simulated write. It can also pass where the live run fails (validation, uniqueness, required fields). Drop the equivalence claim and say the failure is the dry run's own.
6. **should-fix. What a simulated row holds is not checkable.** "A later read by id of a row the run created or updated answers the simulated values." For an updated live row: the live row with the simulated fields laid over it, or only the fields the node set? For a created row: fields the engine sets on a real insert (defaults, autonumber, formula, owner, timestamps) are absent, which changes a later decision that reads them; say so. The order asked for this representation to be stated.
7. nit. `dryRun` takes no name while `registerFlow` takes one; say that the definition's own `name` is the one registration judges and nodes read (the per-flow translation keys).
8. nit. `tenantId` is the one caller-supplied scope key left in the options; say whether it must be a tenant the named user belongs to, since the "no grants" rationale does not cover it.
9. nit. `FlowDryRunStopStep.reason: 'pause'` on a `subflow` or `map` names a property of the descriptor, not what the node would do; `FlowDryRunDecisionStep.expression` is singular while an inclusive decision can have several that held.

Readings beyond the order:

- `script` as outbound: right. The executor calls a registered function that can write anything, so never calling it is the only reading that keeps "without changing live data".
- `subflow` and `map` stop: accepted as the conservative reading. The child is a different, registered definition that may be `runAs: 'system'`, and simulating it is a later widening. The rule is checkable (`supportsPause: true`, both descriptors declare it).
- `not_simulated` stop for an unnamed node type: right in principle (unknown effect), subject to finding 3.
- `'failed'` status: right to add (the ruling says a refused node is not skipped silently), subject to finding 5.
- Simulated writes not judged by validation, uniqueness or required fields: right, and honestly stated; the permission exception beside it is finding 2.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f635d5af49fa982a9b4f1c2aed1feab34d2cf646`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-dry-run.pin.test.ts

DELTA review from `0695d5ce8169a39f13dbda89a6f9b9ffdf68609e` (record ID: 6893425750) to this head, judged against the seat ruling 6893433747 on card #33757. Taken over under handoff 6894111357; claim 6894148564. Tier evidence: `verify-review-tier.mjs` passes on this reviewer's own transcript, every turn at the tier; no other agent was run.

Read, not reviewed (outside the diff, on the head's tree): `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts` (`execute`, `validateNodeInputSchemas`), `dag-traversal.ts`, `builtin/parallel-node.ts`, `builtin/map-node.ts`, the `supportsPause` declarations, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` (`canWriteObject`), `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts`. The changeset and the two generated baselines are the lane seat's ACCEPT; the baselines are read in ① because the order asked for it.

### ① Derived judgments

- The merge: `bd969ec5` has parents `0695d5ce` and `1e65a389`. The head's tree differs from `1e65a389` in exactly the PR's five files, 643 lines added and none removed, so nothing of main was lost or altered. Right.
- The generated baselines: at the merge commit the two `contracts.json` files carried the branch side (the `merge=os-regen` paths) and so lacked the seven names main added in #33725; `f635d5af` regenerates them. At the head each file is main's at `1e65a389` plus exactly 14 entries and no removal; the 14 are the 14 `export interface` / `export type` declarations the diff adds to `automation-service.ts`, name and kind matching one for one, and each origin points at that file. Right. Nothing was regenerated here; the head's own gates (Build Core, Lint and Repo Gates, Type Check) are green.
- Main has moved past `1e65a389`; it has not touched these two baselines or `automation-service.ts` since, and a trial merge of the head with current main is conflict-free.
- Check-runs on the head: every run is completed, `success` or `skipped`. The PR is a draft, so no auto-merge is armed.
- The surface is additive against main: one optional member, 14 exported types, no existing member, type or code changed. `FLOW_NO_START_NODE` left a union that was never published.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch with `Metadata-protocol: none` still matches the diff (no authorable key). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The `runAs: 'system'` refusal is unchanged on this head and is not re-opened here; it goes to the maintainer through #33661, as the ruling says.
- The PR author is the fleet bot; no off-relay write to name.
- No SQL, no id materialisation: types and doc only.
- The PR body's round-2 line for F1 says the method doc places the start condition "as `execute` does". It does not; see S10. That line is prose and the lane seat's to correct with the fix.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, item by item against record 6893425750 and the ruling:

- **F1: closed.** `'condition_not_met'` is a status of its own, `startCondition` carries the authored condition and `result: false`, set exactly on that status, with no steps. The engine exit it names exists as described (`engine.ts` L7711 to L7731 on this tree). Its place in the answer order is S10 below, a new finding on text this round added.
- **F2: closed.** `FlowDryRunWritePermission` is three-way and required on every write step; `'allowed'` and `'refused'` are bound to `canWriteObject` (insert, update), `'not_judged'` covers every delete, and the type's doc says the row-level and post-image rules, controlled-by-parent, the tenant post-image, provenance gates and the `owner_id` forge are never reported. That list agrees with what `canWriteObject`'s own doc disclaims. "`'not_judged'` never means allowed" is stated in both places, and the round-1 promise of a `refusal` for any permission refusal is gone.
- **F3: closed.** `parallel` replaces the two gateway ids. Measured on this tree: `parallel-node.ts` flattens the per-branch step sinks in `config.branches` order; an inclusive decision's conditioned edges run one at a time in edge order (`dag-traversal.ts` L736 to L752); unconditional out-edges run under `Promise.all` (L786 to L793). The contract's rule, branch by branch in declaration order with each branch's steps together, is deterministic and makes no false claim about the live log. For unconditional fan-out that order is the dry run's own; the reading is accepted (N13).
- **F4: closed.** `FlowDryRunRefusalCode` is the two codes; the type's doc says why the third is absent, and the `execute` exit is the defensive one registration makes unreachable (L7699 to L7708).
- **F5: closed.** `'failed'` reads "could not continue past a step", the equivalence claim is gone, and both directions are named in the status doc and in the method doc.
- **F6: closed.** An updated row reads as the live row with the simulated fields laid over it; a deleted row reads as nothing; a created row holds only the fields the flow set, with the engine-set fields named as absent.
- **N7: closed.** The definition's own `name` is the one registration judges and nodes read their per-flow keys under; no registered flow of that name is read or touched.
- **N8: closed.** The reading is accepted: a `tenantId` the named user is not a member of is refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED`, before admission, and the options doc says the refusal is the dry run's own. Measured: run setup refuses no organization, and `resolveUserAuthzGrants` fills `org_user_ids` for whatever `tenantId` it is handed (L2494 to L2504), so without this refusal a non-member would read that organization's member list.
- **N9: closed.** The six stop reasons name what the node would do (`'starts_flow'` for `subflow` and `map`, `'suspends'` for any other `supportsPause: true` type); `expressions` is a list. On this tree `supportsPause: true` is declared by `screen`, `wait`, `subflow`, `map` and the two approval nodes only, so no outbound type falls in both classes.

New on this head:

**S10 (should-fix) — the answer order ranks the input-schema refusal ahead of the start condition, and the doc says the live run evaluates the condition at the same point. It does not.** "In what order it answers" lists `FLOW_INPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID` (third bullet) before the start condition (fourth bullet), and the fourth bullet says the dry run "mirrors the live run's skip exit, which evaluates the same condition at the same point". In `execute` the start condition is evaluated first (`engine.ts` L7724) and `validateNodeInputSchemas`, the only producer of that code, runs after it and after the re-entrancy guard (L7787). So for a definition with a node input-schema violation and a record the condition does not hold for, the live run answers the skip and the contract as written answers `status: 'refused'`. The implementer of #33661 must either contradict this text or keep an order `execute` does not have, and changing which answer wins after publication is a change to a published contract. Either swap the two bullets so the condition is judged first, as `execute` does, or keep the order, drop "at the same point" and say the order is the dry run's own. Move the pin and the PR body line with it.

Nits, to fold into the same push:

- N11 (nit): the method doc says a `'refused'` write "is a refusal the step met", so its step carries `refusal`; the pin's `failedOnPermission` fixture has `permission: 'refused'` and no `refusal`.
- N12 (nit): the method doc's "`'not_judged'` for every delete and for every refusal that check does not judge" can be read as an insert or update step carrying `'not_judged'`; the type's doc is the precise one (an insert or update is `'allowed'` or `'refused'`, the rest is never reported). Align the sentence. Neither place says what a write step answers when no object-level check is installed.
- N13 (nit): the step-order text does not say that, for unconditional fan-out, the list is the dry run's own order and can differ from the live step log, as F5 says for `'failed'`.

`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-dry-run.pin.test.ts`: it pins the five statuses, the two codes, the three permissions (required), the six stop reasons, `startCondition`, `expressions` and the new doc sentences, and agrees with the contract apart from N11. It pins no sentence of the answer order, which is why S10 passes it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5753362e87b135179c2a4067fd5cb27e1a459b57`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-dry-run.pin.test.ts

Read at 2026-11-15T13:26Z. Claim: comment 6894964098. Handed to review#2 by review#1 (6894943447 on mailbox #33873). DELTA review from `f635d5af49fa982a9b4f1c2aed1feab34d2cf646` (record ID: 6894214508, FAIL on S10) to this head, judged against the seat ruling 6894244795 on card #33757. One commit sits on top, `5753362e`; `git diff f635d5af 5753362e` touches the two scope files only (63 lines added, 29 removed), so the changeset and the two generated baselines are byte-identical to the previous head.

Read, not reviewed (outside the diff, on the head's tree): `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts` (`execute`, `executeKey`, its catch, `validateNodeInputSchemas`), `dag-traversal.ts` (`evaluateCondition`, the edge traversal), `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` (`canWriteObject`), `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`, `packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts` (`FlowInnerRefusalSchema`). The changeset and the generated baselines are the lane seat's ACCEPT.
